text.tspan: How a DNS query reaches Route 53 (the authoritative name server)
Root name server (managed by IANA, part of ICANN)
TLD name server (.com, run by the registry)
Anatomy of a name: http :// api . www . example . com .
FQDN (fully qualified domain name) = api.www.example.com. (every label up to the root)
2. DNS routing: authoritative DNS for your
hosted zones; you update the records
• Registry: owns a TLD, keeps its database
• Zone file / hosted zone: holds the DNS records
• Name server: answers DNS queries; either
• Records: A, AAAA, CNAME, NS, MX, TXT, ...
